Our Election Infrastructure Security Timeline continues to grow — and these two developments are particularly significant because they involve the federal government's cybersecurity and national-security infrastructure.

🇺🇸 SEPTEMBER 22 — PENTAGON DIRECTS NSA + CYBER COMMAND TO PROTECT THE MIDTERMS

According to the Associated Press, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth signed a directive ordering the military's cyber and intelligence apparatus to prioritize protection of the 2026 midterm elections from foreign interference and cyber threats.

The directive involves:

➡️ National Security Agency (NSA)
➡️ U.S. Cyber Command
➡️ Other Defense Department intelligence/cyber elements
➡️ Coordination with DHS and other federal agencies

Military cyber involvement in election protection isn't entirely new. The federal government has treated election systems as critical infrastructure since 2017.

But this is a specific 2026 directive mobilizing defense cyber and intelligence capabilities ahead of November.

And then, just TWO DAYS LATER...

🛡️ SEPTEMBER 24 — CISA RELEASES ITS 2026 ELECTION INFRASTRUCTURE SECURITY PLAN

DHS's Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency published a formal 13-page security plan for the 2026 election.

The plan addresses threats including:

💻 Software vulnerabilities
🗄️ Attacks against voter-registration databases
⚠️ Insider threats
🏛️ Physical threats against election facilities and polling locations
📡 Cyber threats against election infrastructure

CISA says its support for state and local election officials includes:

➡️ Threat-intelligence sharing
➡️ Vulnerability scanning
➡️ Risk assessments
➡️ Cybersecurity assistance
➡️ Training and exercises
➡️ Election-system resilience measures

Now look at the timing:

📍 SEPT. 22 — Pentagon directive
NSA + Cyber Command + defense intelligence directed to counter foreign election threats.

⬇️ 48 HOURS

📍 SEPT. 24 — CISA election-security plan
DHS publishes its operational framework for protecting election infrastructure.

Because the federal election-security activity we're tracking now spans:

🇺🇸 DOJ — investigations & prosecutions

🇺🇸 SUPREME COURT — determining what measures can proceed

The scope of the federal activity has expanded considerably since July 16.
